newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ships rise on dividend resumption report.
newsitem.headline: Japan ships rise on dividend resumption report.

text.p: Shares in Japan shipping lines 0#SHP.T rose in Tuesday morning trade, encouraged by a newspaper report that the firms are likely to resume dividend payments in the year to end-March 1998, brokers said.
As of 0136 GMT, Navix Line Ltd had added 19 yen to trade at 224 with volume of 3.72 million shares, the fifth most heavily traded issue on the Tokyo bourse.
Mitsui O.S.K. Lines Ltd also gained, with trade totalling 3.63 million shares, rising 22 yen to 260. Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha Ltd rose 21 yen to 270.
The companies will probably pay an annual dividend of three to four yen per share in 1997/98, the first dividend payments in years, the Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Tuesday.

Shipping line operators' earnings performance has improved as a result of restructuring measures, including a cut in the number of Japanese sailors, and the weak yen, which boosted their international competitiveness, the financial daily added.
Shipping firm officials declined to comment on the report.
